turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): morning. she was chatting in the passage. naledi, what number did you tell me?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Nineteen.
[SEG0003] person_3 (DOCTOR): right, we'll see what the scale says. so what's the matter?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Eye.
[SEG0005] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): shame, doc, sticky red eye. the school wants a sick note, otherwise they won't have her tomorrow.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): okay. one eye or both, and how long?

[SEG0007] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): left one first, about four days, thursday. then the right one started, umm, i actually can't say if that was yesterday or the day before. both are red now, stuck shut in the morning.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): this came after a cold?
[SEG0009] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): ja, last week. snotty nose and a bit of cough. the nose is pretty much gone, the cough still pitches up at night.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): naledi, does the eye hurt?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): itchy at all?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0014] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): she rubs it the whole time though. and she sleeps badly, tossing for half the night.
[SEG0015] person_3 (DOCTOR): naledi, are you sleeping okay?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes.
[SEG0017] person_3 (DOCTOR): hm. mom says half the night, you say you're fine. were you hot this morning?
[SEG0018] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): ja, uh, i thought so. checked with our thermometer.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Thirty eight.
[SEG0020] person_1 (NURSE): she did say thirty eight, that was the home reading. mine just now is 36.8. pulse 104. and she said nineteen, the scale comes out at 19.2 kilograms.
[SEG0021] person_3 (DOCTOR): so 36.8, the fever has settled. any problems with the tummy or the waterworks?
[SEG0022] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no, all fine. she's eating.
[SEG0023] person_3 (DOCTOR): what medicine has she had?
[SEG0024] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): panado syrup by mouth, the paracetomol. i give 7.5 ml three times a day when she's hot. gave it this morning still.
[SEG0025] person_1 (NURSE): the bottle in the bag, the sticker says 5 ml, not 7.5. i read it twice.
[SEG0026] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): the sister at the clinic said 7.5 for her weight. so i've been pouring 7.5.
[SEG0027] person_3 (DOCTOR): err, the sticker says one thing, the clinic sister another. i won't pin a dose down off that. does she take it every day?
[SEG0028] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): except sundays. she will not take the tablets, ag no, the syrup, she spits it on sundays at her gran's.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Saturday.
[SEG0030] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): ag, saturday, not sunday. gran has her on saturdays. i mixed the days up.
[SEG0031] person_3 (DOCTOR): saturday, got it. any allergy to medicines or eye drops?
[SEG0032] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no. nothing.

[SEG0033] person_3 (DOCTOR): chin up, let me look. mm, both whites are pink, left more than the right, with yellow crust on the lashes. the cornea is clear and the lids aren't really swollen. pupils are fine.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Itchy.
[SEG0035] person_3 (DOCTOR): ah, itchy. so it is itchy, even though you said no earlier. the rubbing fits with that.
[SEG0036] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): oh, and the graze on her knee, from the bike at school. healed in five days, just a mark, no oozing.

[SEG0037] person_3 (DOCTOR): five days, that's normal healing, not a slow healer. i'm thinking viral conjunctivitis after the cold, though i can't completely rule out a bacterial one. no pain, both eyes, clear cornea, so no antibiotic, and chloramphenicol ointment won't hurry a virus.
[SEG0038] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): no drops then? what about the school, they were quite sharp on the phone.

[SEG0039] person_3 (DOCTOR): no drops. wash hands, her own face cloth, wipe the crust with cooled boiled water, no sharing towels. i'll do the sick note, keep her home tomorrow, and she can go back the day after if the goo is less. come back if the eye gets sore, if the clear bit goes cloudy, if a lid swells, or if it's not settling in a week.
[SEG0040] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): okay. the parking was a nightmare, but thanks doc.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Bye.
[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): cheers naledi. sister will print the note at reception.

spec.situation: Parent with a child with red sticky eye after a cold; school wants a note; one eye then both; no eye pain; doctor advises hygiene, no antibiotic, explains return advice.

traps.happens: A caregiver or relative reports observations ('the cut healed in five days', 'she sleeps badly', 'he does not take the tablets on Sundays'); the patient agrees, disagrees or corrects one point. The nurse also reports a measurement that the patient mentioned before.
traps.label_rule: reported_by follows who said it. A healing cut that healed normally is a negative finding (no slow-healing wounds) or nothing, NOT a symptom. A disputed fact is recorded with certainty disputed or as an uncertainty. A correction replaces the earlier value (Saturday, not Sunday).

features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.
disputed_numbers: the nurse reads a value and the patient or relative disagrees or remembers another (a dose, a weight, a BP). Keep both and record an uncertainty.

bad.reason: Resolved fever supported, but onset 'this morning' is not stated.
